description: Wavetable oscillator read by a phasor rather than by its own pitch: the input voltage reads straight across one wave of a wavetable loaded from a WAV file

params.text: Sweeps through the waves of the loaded wavetable, from the first wave at 0% to the last at 100%, crossfading between neighbouring waves on the way
Scales the Position CV jack below, -100% to +100%, inverting it below 0; at 0 the jack has no effect at all
Unipolar lifts the output by 5V so it runs 0 to 10V; Bipolar leaves it running -5V to +5V
LFO reads the wavetable as it is, with no antialiasing; VCO picks a bandlimited copy of the wave to suit how fast the phasor is moving, which keeps aliasing down at audio rates

inputs.text: A ramp from 0V to 10V reads once straight across the wave; the voltage is divided by 10 and wrapped, so anything outside 0 to 10V comes back round rather than stopping at the end
Added to the Position knob after the trimpot above it scales the voltage, with 10V covering the whole wavetable at a full trimpot; the total is held between the first and last wave

outputs.text: The wave read at the phasor's position, running -5V to +5V, or 0 to 10V with the Offset switch set to Unipolar

notes: a phasor drives this, not a pitch: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO saw. With nothing patched in, the output holds a steady voltage.
the display shows the name of the loaded wavetable and the wave now being read. A WAV file dropped onto it is loaded straight away; the display itself cannot be clicked for help.
the module comes up with a built-in four-wave table called Basic.wav, holding a sine, a triangle, a sawtooth and a square. A loaded wavetable is saved into the patch and travels with it.
menu: Mode: LFO (no antialiasing), VCO (antialiased) — the same choice as the Mode switch on the panel
Initialize wavetable — replaces whatever is loaded with the built-in sine, triangle, sawtooth and square
Load wavetable — opens a file dialogue for a WAV, AIFF or raw sample file to read as the wavetable
Save wavetable — writes the loaded wavetable out as a WAV file
Wave points: 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — sets how many samples make up one wave, and so where the loaded file is cut into separate waves

bipolar · continuous · polyphonic
